metadata.case_name: CHAN KAI MAN v. BAIQIAN INTERNATIONAL HOLDING LTD

plaintiff.occupation_after: Cross-border lorry driver (employed by Uni-Link Logistics Ltd. since July 2014)
plaintiff.education_level: education in Mainland China up to level 5 in primary school

injuries.description: soft tissue injury to his low back; back sprain resulting in residual pain
source: Both Dr Lam and Dr Chiang agreed that Chan suffered soft tissue injury to his low back which injury was consistent with the mechanism of injury described if the Accident did happen.
Chan was assessed to have sustained back sprain resulting in residual pain.
injuries.icd_description: Strain or sprain of lumbar spine

manifestations.description: tenderness and stiffness over the 2nd and 3rd lumbar paraspinal muscle
markedly limited range of spinal movement in flexion
right buttock numbness on prolonged sitting

treatments_received.treatment: Consultation at Hui Kok Yin Bone Injuries Clinic (許國賢骨傷科醫館) on 3 August 2012
source: he went to consult a Chinese medical practitioner in 許國賢骨傷科醫館 (Hui Kok Yin Bone Injuries Clinic) on 3 August 2012.

treatments_received.treatment: Accident & Emergency Department treatment at Queen Mary Hospital on 4 August 2012 (given analgesics, X-ray lumbar spine showed no fracture, discharged with two days sick leave)
source: Due to intensifying pain, Chan went to the Accident & Emergency Department of Queen Mary Hospital for treatment at about 4 am of 4 August 2012. It was recorded in the medical certificate dated 15 October 2012 issued by Dr Herbert Yuen, resident of the Accident & Emergency Department, Queen Mary Hospital, that Chan complained of lower back pain, but there was no lower limb numbness or weakness, and that he was alert and afebrile. X-ray of lumbar spine showed no fracture. He was given analgesics and discharged with two days sick leave granted to him.

treatments_received.treatment: Consultations at Sai Ying Pun Clinic (Family Medicine) on 22, 24 and 28 August 2012, and 3 and 5 September 2012; referred to physiotherapy
source: Chan subsequently attended the Sai Ying Pun Clinic (Family Medicine) (“SYPC”) for consultation and treatment for 5 times on 22, 24 and 28 August 2012, and 3 and 5 September 2012. Medical report dated 22 October 2012 compiled by Dr Ngai Ming Leon, resident in Sai Ying Pun Clinic (Family Medicine), Department of Family Medicine & Primary Healthcare, Hospital Authority, recorded that Chan claimed that his back was sprained on 2 August 2012 when he was pulling heavy objects. When Chan first attended SYPC on 22 August 2012, he complained about having persistent back pain. Numbness on his right foot without any weakness was noted. Physical examination revealed tenderness and stiffness over the 2nd and 3rd lumbar paraspinal muscle and the range of spinal movement was markedly limited in flexion. Though there was decreased sensation over the whole right foot, its power was not affected. Doctor’s diagnosis was back sprain and radiculopathy. Chan was referred to physiotherapy. He was discharged with oral analgesics.

treatments_received.treatment: Medical treatment in Dongguan City (January, March and October 2013)
source: It also appears from the medical receipts produced by Chan that he had sought medical treatment in Dongguan City in January, March and October 2013.

treatments_received.treatment: Joint medical assessment by Dr Lam and Dr Chiang on 16 January 2014; joint report dated 10 April 2014
source: On 16 January 2014, a joint medical assessment was carried out on Chan by Dr Lam Chi Keung Johnson appointed by Chan’s solicitors and Dr Chiang Si Chung Arthur appointed by BQIH’s solicitors. Dr Lam and Dr Chiang submitted a joint report dated 10 April 2014 (“the Joint Report”).

losses.description: pain, suffering and loss of amenities
